implementationRisks.title: Existing protected reads do not implement the revised persisted relationship and institute boundaries

sourceEvidence.explanation: The current handler checks only selected role strings. A supplied specific courseId is accepted directly, and subsequent enrollment, syllabus, and submission queries use that ID without proving instructor ownership or institute membership. INSTRUCTOR is also absent from the accepted aliases.

The current handler trusts the requested institute code and returns announcements for every course in that institute without constraining courses by the actor's enrollment, assignment, or Admin authority.
The courseId branch reads syllabus items before resolving the course and proving the actor's enrollment, assignment, institute, or Admin authority.

The institute branch does not bind the requested institute to a non-Admin actor's home institute, treats every non-STUDENT role as an instructor, and does not implement the matrix's system-wide Admin enumeration.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implementation, authenticated users—including SUPER_USER or unknown roles in some branches—can reach private course, announcement, assignment, grade, and student-risk data outside the revised COURSE_READ/TEACH boundaries.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement the specified canonical actor resolution and fail-closed role classification before protected input parsing, then constrain the first database query by the persisted course institute and the exact Admin, assigned-instructor, or approved-enrollment relationship. Resolve specific course IDs before child queries and return the specified safe 404 for foreign or non-owned resources.

implementationRisks.title: Existing own-account routes do not enforce the Super User support ceiling

sourceEvidence.explanation: Any session accepted by getSession can read the request body and change its user's password; there is no explicit recognized-role check or pre-parse SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial.
Any session accepted by getSessionFromRequest has its expiry extended and receives identity data; there is no explicit SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial before the session mutation.

implementationRisks.impact: The unimplemented baseline lets SUPER_USER use password and session-management capabilities that the revised design limits to login, logout, and /api/auth/me.
implementationRisks.recommendation: After canonical authentication, classify the actor using the revised fail-closed role model and return 403 for SUPER_USER or UNKNOWN before parsing account-management input, reading password data, extending a session, or performing any mutation.

implementationRisks.title: Existing recovery flow can create password-reset credentials for a Super User account

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler finds a target solely by email and creates an OTP without checking whether the target is an active SUPER_USER.
The generated OTP is logged and may be returned in non-production, but no Super User target denial precedes those disclosures.

implementationRisks.impact: Until remediated, the public recovery protocol can initiate account-management access for SUPER_USER, contradicting the exact basic-support ceiling and increasing the risk of oversight-account takeover.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Preserve the non-enumerating public response while checking the persisted target role and active state server-side; for an active SUPER_USER, perform no OTP invalidation, creation, logging, response disclosure, or email side effect.

implementationRisks.title: Existing login and identity support do not fail closed for unknown roles or implement explicit Super User login handling

sourceEvidence.explanation: Only ADMIN is distinguished. Every other persisted role, including SUPER_USER and unknown values, follows the generic non-Admin institute branch and can receive a newly created session.
The response returns the persisted role and institute but contains no explicit recognized-role rejection or Super User destination/support handling.
The handler returns identity for every active session accepted by the resolver without rejecting an unknown persisted role.

implementationRisks.impact: Unknown roles can become session-bearing actors, and Super User login behavior remains dependent on legacy generic role handling rather than the revised explicit support contract.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Classify the persisted role before session creation and protected identity serialization; reject UNKNOWN, explicitly admit SUPER_USER only for the defined support capability, preserve the existing home-portal credential check, and keep post-login destination selection separate from credential validation.

implementationRisks.title: Existing registration logic explicitly blocks only ADMIN and defaults other accepted role values to STUDENT

sourceEvidence.explanation: The route-level privileged-role check rejects ADMIN only; protection against SUPER_USER and other unknown values depends entirely on the external schema.
After schema parsing, every role other than exact INSTRUCTOR is silently mapped to STUDENT, contrary to the revised rule that invalid roles must not normalize into a granted role.

implementationRisks.impact: If the schema admits a new or unexpected role value, registration may silently grant STUDENT instead of failing closed; the route itself does not establish that SUPER_USER can never be selected.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Use an explicit public-registration allowlist for STUDENT and INSTRUCTOR, reject ADMIN, SUPER_USER, UNKNOWN, and all unrecognized values before hashing or database access, and remove the catch-all conversion to STUDENT.

implementationRisks.title: Existing logout does not use the canonical one-actor credential-selection contract

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler extracts a Bearer token directly and passes it to deleteSession without canonical cookie-first resolution or actor/session binding.
A supplied tokenOverride takes precedence over the cookie session, so a request containing both credentials does not follow the revised valid-cookie precedence rule.

implementationRisks.impact: Cookie/Bearer conflict behavior can revoke a different session than the canonical actor's selected session, undermining deterministic support semantics and conflict-case verification.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Resolve exactly one authenticated session using the canonical cookie-first, Bearer-fallback rule and revoke that selected session only; retain transitional session-ID compatibility within that resolver.

implementationRisks.title: Required operational trust assignments remain absent and block production disclosure

sourceEvidence.symbol: META-01 exact disclosure and operational contract
sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied design states that the trusted academic/privacy approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset identity/fingerprint and attestation procedure, expiry lifetime owner, and revocation publication/runbook owner are required human or operator assignments and are not supplied.

implementationRisks.impact: No production metadata approval can be trusted or admitted until these identities and procedures are assigned. Production oversight reads must remain deny-by-default; an implementation or architecture PASS cannot authorize disclosure.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Before deployment, governance must name the required approver and maintainer, bind the actual production dataset/environment fingerprint, choose expiry policy, and assign a coordinated revocation publication runbook. Do not invent identities or use fixture bindings for production.

coverage.assessment: The revised TEACH design requires canonical authentication, explicit instructor aliases or Admin, persisted course assignment and institute binding, child resolution through authorized courses, safe 404 for foreign courses, and SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial before protected parsing and reads. The design is sufficiently specific; the current handler does not implement it.

The revised COURSE_READ design requires institute-scoped enumeration constrained in-query to Admin authority, assigned instructor courses, or approved student enrollments, with SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denied first. The design closes the current institute-wide disclosure without requiring a caller-supplied courseId.

Both courseId and institute enumeration branches are covered by the revised COURSE_READ contract. Specific courses must be resolved and authorized before syllabus reads; institute listings must use persisted enrollment, assignment, or Admin scope and fail closed for unknown roles.
The revised OWN boundary expressly excludes SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN from password management and requires denial before parsing or mutation while preserving legitimate normal-role self-service.

The revised PUBLIC_AUTH contract preserves anonymous recovery behavior but requires an active-SUPER_USER target to be denied before any reset mutation or disclosure. The design is adequate; implementation remains absent.

OPTIONS remains a capability-free CORS protocol. POST explicitly supports recognized active roles including SUPER_USER, rejects UNKNOWN, preserves home-portal validation, and separates the Super User's ICS post-login destination from credential authorization.

OPTIONS remains capability-free. POST is an allowed Super User support operation, but the future implementation must bind revocation to the single canonically selected real session and cover cookie/Bearer conflicts.

OPTIONS remains capability-free. GET is explicitly allowed to return only the authenticated actor's own identity, including SUPER_USER, using the canonical resolver; UNKNOWN remains unauthorized and selected-institute mutation is forbidden.
The revised OWN policy preserves normal-role own-session refresh but explicitly denies SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN before mutation, consistent with the exact support ceiling.

OPTIONS remains capability-free. POST preserves anonymous registration while requiring an explicit public-role allowlist and rejecting ADMIN, SUPER_USER, UNKNOWN, and invalid roles without silent normalization.

limitations: This is a document-only pre-implementation architecture assessment. No source modifications, tests, runtime execution, database operations, transaction exercise, deployment validation, or formal gate acceptance were performed or claimed.
Only the ten assigned route paths and their fourteen assigned HTTP methods were reviewed. Shared policy and helper excerpts were considered solely where necessary to assess those assigned boundaries.
The packet supplies no separately enumerated acceptance-criteria identifiers beyond its operation IDs and named contracts; affectedAC therefore uses the exact assigned HTTP operation IDs.

Line-numbered content for 008-revised-super-user-architecture.md was not supplied; evidence against that document is necessarily anchored to its exact section symbol rather than fabricated line positions.
Runtime behavior of imported schemas, CORS, rate-limit, mail, reward, and session helpers was not independently executed. Risks are based only on the supplied sanitized content.

Operational approver, maintainer, production dataset/fingerprint, expiry-owner, and revocation-runbook assignments are absent. The design's deny-by-default rule makes this an explicit deployment blocker rather than an unresolved design defect.
